headline: Entropy commissions Glacier co-generation carbon capture project in Alberta
summary: Entropy Inc. (Advantage Energy) commissioned its Glacier co-generation CCS project in Saddle Hills County, Alberta, adding a 15 MW co-gen turbine with integrated capture and targeting ~192,000 tpa of CO2 captured and sequestered at capture rates above 90%; billed as first-of-kind low-carbon natural gas and low-carbon power.
co2crc_note: A commissioned post-combustion capture co-gen unit with a multi-year operating record is a useful reference point for gas-processing CCS economics relevant to Australian operators.
extractor_note: Announced 30 Jul North American time; lands 31 Jul Melbourne, inside the Monday window that opens Friday.

headline: Heidelberg hails piling progress at Padeswood cement carbon capture plant, Wales
summary: Heidelberg Materials reported more than 600 piles installed at its Padeswood cement CCS facility in Flintshire, north Wales, with ~60,000 t of aggregate laid and 25,000 t of topsoil removed; the plant is designed to capture ~95% of the works' CO2 (~800,000 tpa) with CO2 routed via HyNet to Liverpool Bay storage, and is due operational in 2029. EPC is delivered by Worley and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.
co2crc_note: First cement-works CCS in the UK moving into construction; a cement-sector reference for Australian hard-to-abate decarbonisation pathways.

headline: Energy Intelligence: uncertainty plagues US DAC sector as players shift strategy
summary: An Energy Intelligence analysis charts the US direct-air-capture sector bifurcating amid policy uncertainty — a freeze on the DOE's $3.5bn DAC Hubs programme and a proposed 45Q cut from $180 to $36/t for DAC — with buyers and developers concentrating in California, New York and Washington, well-capitalised integrated players such as Occidental proving resilient, and Canada and Kenya emerging as alternative DAC destinations.
co2crc_note: US policy-driven DAC retrenchment reshapes the global CDR investment map and where capital and offtake demand flow — relevant to Australian CDR positioning.

headline: Sinopec Qilu-Shengli CCUS project passes 2.4 Mt cumulative CO2 stored
summary: Sinopec reported that by end-June 2026 its million-tonne-scale Qilu Petrochemical-Shengli Oilfield CCUS project — China's first full-chain megatonne CCUS demonstration — had cumulatively captured and sequestered more than 2.4 million tonnes of CO2, with daily EOR oil output in the demonstration area rising from 220 to 506 tonnes.
co2crc_note: China's flagship full-chain CCUS-EOR demonstration continues to accrue stored volumes; a benchmark for large-scale operational learning.
extractor_note: Radar: 29 Jul, out of today's window.

headline: Uniper selects SLB Capturi capture technology for Connah's Quay power CCS
summary: SLB Capturi was selected as preferred carbon-capture technology licensor for Uniper's proposed Connah's Quay Low Carbon Power project in Deeside, Wales, deploying its amine-based Big Catch technology; captured CO2 would feed the HyNet network for offshore storage. This distinct technology-licensor selection follows the earlier Worley EPC award already briefed.
co2crc_note: Technology-licensor selection for a gas-plus-capture power project; a marker of the amine-capture supply chain for flexible power.
extractor_note: Radar: 28 Jul, out of today's window.
